0.label: left_rim_crocodile_strip
0.description: A tall strip of the tray's left rim containing a net-patterned block, a long crocodile or monitor lizard with cross-hatched skin running down the rim, small creatures and a coiled spiral in the bottom corner.
0.iconography: The crocodile is the rim's largest animal — water power and danger (Olókun). The coiled spiral at the corner belongs to the serpent / renewal family. One strip of a four-sided programme, not a single motif.

panel.title: Rectangular Modakeke Ifá tray: face flanked by scorpions, tortoise at the foot
panel.summary: A rectangular Ifá tray with a plain field framed by a crowded carved border. A face with cheek marks sits at the top centre between two scorpion- or crab-like creatures; a round disc with a cross, like a tortoise shell, marks the centre of the foot; crocodile, birds, fish and figures fill the sides.

register_readings.reading: Top (undetected): corner knot, net blocks, two segmented clawed creatures (scorpions or crabs) flanking the face with ilà marks.
Left side: a crocodile with cross-hatched skin and a spiral at the corner.
Right side (undetected): a bird, a large fish or leaf form, and a figure with a crested head.
Foot (undetected): a round cross-marked disc with radiating edges (tortoise shell or sun) between beaded bars, with quadrupeds and a long object that may be a gun at the right.

panel.composition: Four-sided frame with a marked top (face) and foot (disc), each flanked symmetrically; the sides are crowded and less symmetrical.
panel.narrative: A full Ifá cosmos around the working field: Ẹ̀ṣù's face at the head, dangerous creatures (scorpions, crocodile) beside him, a tortoise shell or sun disc at the foot, and birds, fish and people along the sides. The tortoise (Ìjàpá) is a trickster and offering animal; scorpions and crocodile read as the dangers a sacrifice averts.
panel.hypotheses: Does not bear on 'chronicle'. Not numerical.
cross_panel_links: Crocodile on the rim: KBA_10300 (drawn tray), FoA_04-5585.

uncertainties: Only the left strip is detected; the rest is read from the photograph.
The top creatures could be tortoises or crabs rather than scorpions.
